name: init_score_wave_display_state
description: Sets one byte and two words of state to fixed starting values, then makes a fixed sequence of subroutine calls, including one with two constant coordinates and a final call with a constant position and size. The referenced strings score and wave show it initialises the score and wave display.

name: wait_status_then_finish
description: Repeatedly polls a status routine. Once it returns zero, a closing routine is called and the function returns; inside the loop, two further checks decide whether polling continues.

name: load_bitmap_file_into_struct
description: Opens a named file in old-file mode, reads a 10-byte header for the dimensions, allocates a buffer sized from them, reads the pixel data into it and closes the file. It then stores the dimensions, row stride and buffer pointers in the caller's structure, or calls a failure routine if the open fails.

name: load_planar_image_deinterleaved
description: Opens a named file, reads a 10-byte header and allocates a buffer, then reads the pixel data and splits each group of four source words into four separate plane rows. It writes all-ones marker words at the start and end of each row before storing the result in the caller's structure.

name: blit_clipped_sprite_five_passes
description: Clips a sprite rectangle against stored screen bounds and adjusts the source pointers and shift for any clipped left or top edge. It then programs the blitter registers for five successive passes, waiting for the blitter to be free before each one.

name: init_shape_tables_from_file
description: Loads the file named shapes/trumpet, then fills a five-entry table of row offsets and half-widths from its header. It fills two 12-entry tables with values returned by a routine, and a 120-byte table with a routine's results divided by 129.

name: index_first_and_third_chunks
description: Uses a file routine with a fixed identifier to load a buffer, then steps through three consecutive chunk headers. Each size is padded to an even length, and the data offset and length of the first and third chunks are stored in the caller's structure.

name: advance_two_voice_sequencer
description: Runs once per tick and decrements two countdown counters. When a counter expires it reads two command bytes from that voice's stream, sets the next duration from a table (scaled when a flag bit is set) and writes table-derived pitch and length values to shared output words.

name: advance_channel_zero_voice
description: Steps one voice on the first audio channel. When its countdown expires it reads two command bytes, looks up the sample pointer, length and period, and programs them into the channel, then waits a fixed 50-count delay and applies duration scaling from the decoded bits.

name: advance_second_voice_countdown
description: Decrements the countdown for the second voice. When it expires, it reads two command bytes, updates the stored pitch-related state and length, and applies duration scaling; when the countdown is below three it sends a fixed extra value.

name: advance_channel_one_voice
description: Steps one voice on the second audio channel. When its countdown expires it reads two command bytes, looks up a table value for the channel, and writes the channel's pointer, length and volume values, then applies duration scaling from the decoded bits.

name: send_channel_one_low_countdown
description: When the second channel's countdown is below three, it writes a pointer base plus a fixed offset and the constant 2 to shared output words. Otherwise it does nothing.

name: init_voice_state_and_streams
description: Copies two saved stream pointers into the voice state, then clears four state and countdown words. It writes start values to shared output words and sets a flag word to 1.

name: clear_active_flag_state
description: Writes the command value 3 to a shared output word and clears a one-word flag to zero.

name: set_active_flag_state
description: Sets a one-word flag in the shared state to 1 and returns.

name: read_active_flag_state
description: Returns the current value of a one-word flag held in the shared state.

name: dispatch_code_to_handler
description: Takes a code value and returns the result of a shared handler routine for codes 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 19. For any other code it returns the code minus 19.

name: init_tower_level_state
description: Resets a set of score and level state words and fills a 26-entry table of positions with values returned by a routine. It selects a layout offset from a stored counter, counts how many entries of a 49-entry array equal 2, and for counters above two draws several display items at fixed positions. The referenced text about shooting all towers and clearing tower tops shows this is the tower-stage setup.

name: update_and_cull_sprite_list
description: Advances each six-word record in a list: it subtracts a scroll offset from the first word, decrements a timer, adds a velocity-based offset to the third word and nudges the fourth word by an amount returned by a routine. Records whose first word falls below -559 are removed by compacting the list.

name: advance_scrolling_object_frame
description: Advances a frame counter and updates 51 scrolling values by subtracting a speed and wrapping paired offsets within plus or minus 2048. When the first value drops below a threshold the list is shifted and a new entry is generated from a routine result, and periodically five records are swapped and 13 type values are remapped to 3-bit codes.

name: spawn_records_from_table_groups
description: Fills a list of 14-word spawn records from up to five groups of table entries, placing each entry at a column offset set by a stored scroll position and a check based on a routine result. Each record stores its position, a speed that is zero for types 1 and 4 and otherwise depends on the stored scroll position, a type code, and a pointer back to its table entry.

name: draw_entity_by_type
description: Dispatches on a type value, calling a different sequence of drawing routines for types 1, 2, 3 and 5, and a single routine for other values. It then loops over four positions, skipping any whose computed offset is 301 or more, and calls further drawing routines with the entity's coordinates. The available pseudo-code is cut off partway through the loop, so the last draw calls are not visible.

name: spawn_offset_shot_records
description: Scans the spawn records and, for each one of type below three that is not already marked, takes a routine check below 500 before trying three offset positions. When a second routine check passes it claims a new record, marks the source as used and fills the new record with the offset position and a velocity.

name: check_records_for_player_hits
description: Sets a flag from a stored counter, then walks the spawn records and tests each against the player's bounding box. On a hit it calls handler routines with constants, sets the record's state to a hit code and lowers a remaining-count word, and afterwards draws every active record through a routine.

name: cull_offscreen_spawn_records
description: Sets a difficulty-related flag, then scans spawn records from the front and stops at the first one that is not yet due. Expired records are removed by copying the following entry over them and decrementing the count. Once the list ends it looks for a matching record whose timer has run out and sets a countdown and state values.

name: update_velocity_and_sample_offsets
description: Adjusts a vertical velocity word from stored state and routine lookups: it damps the value toward a target, or steps it up and then down, depending on two stored counters. It then looks up two values from that velocity through routines and stores each shifted right by six bits into output words.

name: setup_wave_parameters
description: Computes a scaled difference between two stored positions and draws several values from a routine in fixed ranges, with the second range shrinking as a stored counter rises above 500. It sets a timer to 7 for one of two counters selected by a toggled flag, flips that flag, and calls a shared routine with zero.

name: draw_overlay_items_for_frame
description: Increments a frame counter and draws one or two fixed-size items at computed positions. Horizontal offsets are chosen from a stored flag and bits of the frame counter, and an extra item is drawn when a bit of the flag is set.

name: draw_frame_with_optional_extras
description: Passes the address of a record block to two routines, then runs a per-frame update. It draws two extra items only when a counter exceeds 2, a stored value is below 500 and a flag is clear.

name: run_scroll_transition_loop
description: Returns zero for the first stage. Otherwise it repeatedly scrolls a set of 50 positions, wrapping paired offsets within plus or minus 2048, and waits for each frame until a stored value drops to 5000 or below. It then repeats a waiting loop until a status flag is set and returns that flag.

name: divide_coordinates_by_base_offsets
description: Divides two stored 32-bit coordinate values by a stored base value plus 470 and then by the base plus 730, storing each quotient as a 16-bit word.

name: compute_bounds_quotients_for_param
description: Divides a parameter offset by a value 30720 below and 30720 above it, using divisors built from a stored base plus 470 and plus 730. It stores the four 16-bit quotients in the shared state.

name: divide_values_by_base_offsets_two
description: Divides three stored 32-bit values by a stored base plus 450, and the same three values by the base plus 750, storing six 16-bit quotients.

name: compute_wide_bounds_quotients
description: Stores three 16-bit quotients: a parameter offset by 46080 below and above, each divided by the base plus 750, and the parameter itself divided by the base plus 450.

name: draw_message_text_screen
description: Draws a set of labelled text lines at fixed offsets from a base position and selects one message from an index capped at four. For higher stage values it draws nine messages picked by a routine from a table, then assigns values cycling through 4, 3 and 9 to the flagged entries of a 131-entry array.

name: init_scroll_position_tables
description: Clears several state words and points two base pointers at the scrolling position buffers. It fills two 11-entry tables with values starting at 1 and rising by 1900 per step, with the second table offset by 950.

name: update_scrolling_position_lists
description: Recomputes four scale values from stored state, then scrolls two position lists by a speed. When an entry passes a threshold of -589 it is recycled to the end of the list with 1900 added, and a second list uses -439. It also compacts the record list by dropping records that have moved past -27.

name: draw_block_rows_in_range
description: Chooses a row range from a parameter, then for each row draws one item and sixteen more at coordinates read from a table, using the row value as the vertical position.

name: run_level_end_bonus_sequence
description: Builds a stage-number string, draws a grid of positions and pauses briefly, then runs three passes of twenty frames each. It draws bonus and status text lines, including the stage digit, calls a routine with a value from a stage-indexed table, and finishes with a 100-frame update loop; the referenced text covers the starting and shield bonus messages.

name: check_bounds_and_register_hit
description: Tests a parameter's mask bits against two sets of stored bounds. When the test passes it toggles a state word with a parameter value, sets a flag, calls a routine with 1 and starts an effect with the constant 256.

name: draw_sprite_pattern_by_code
description: Draws a set of primitive items using stored coordinate values. Code 12 uses a twelve-call pattern, code 8 uses a different eight-call pattern, and any other code uses a default eight-call pattern.

name: draw_masked_grid_pairs
description: Computes a base coordinate from a stored value, then for each of four nibbles of a mask it draws pairs of items at offsets from that base and advances the base by a fixed step. It returns the result of the last call made for a set nibble.

name: save_positions_and_set_limit
description: Copies four stored position words into a backup area and calls a routine with a stored value. It then passes the table entry selected by a counter, or a fixed constant when the counter is at least nine, to the same routine.

name: evaluate_trigger_bitfields
description: Clears a countdown when it is active and updates a flag from a stored counter. It then checks up to five 4-bit fields of a mask against stored bounds and, if one matches and a routine check passes, sets a state code of 12, calls a routine and marks the trigger as active.

name: draw_scrolling_sprite_column
description: Draws paired items at coordinates from stored state, then updates a vertical offset and a scale value. It draws a short sequence of four offset pairs using values from a routine, or when a bounds test passes it starts a related routine and marks each active record. The pseudo-code is cut off partway through, so the end of the routine is not visible.

name: advance_records_before_threshold
description: Repeatedly calls a routine and advances a record pointer by six bytes and a stored index by twelve bytes while the head record's key is below the parameter and the pointer stays inside the record list.

name: spawn_and_update_enemy_shots
description: When a mask and a counter allow it, spawns up to two records at fixed offsets from a stored value, gated by routine checks. It then refreshes three routine-derived words for each active record and steps through the records, testing each against a bounds value; on a hit it calls a routine with a constant and then a second routine, and records that pass a limit are marked.

name: draw_periodic_indicator_sprites
description: Draws an indicator at a position chosen by a stored level counter, using a frame counter that cycles from zero to ten and only draws once it passes five. A second branch draws a different indicator when a stored flag and counter are set, and a third draws one of two variants depending on a bit of the frame counter.

name: draw_playfield_and_hit_records
description: Draws a fixed group of items at stored coordinates, then, for each active record in range, tests for a collision with a routine check and calls a routine with a constant on a hit. It then draws records through a routine over a count that depends on the stage counter and steps the record list.

name: transform_points_and_draw_lines
description: Stores a set of coordinate pairs offset from stored values, then passes each pair through two lookup routines and a combining step to scale it. It then issues alternating move and draw calls to connect the transformed points. The pseudo-code is cut off partway through the drawing calls.

name: sweep_scroll_value_across_frames
description: Loops a value from -720 up to zero in steps that change at -360 and -120. For each step it clears a state word, stores a routine-based value, runs a routine with that value and calls two frame routines.

name: run_frames_until_flag_set
description: Runs frames in a loop, clearing a counter each time and waiting for a frame routine to set it, until a status flag or a state flag becomes non-zero. It then picks one of three outcomes from a flag and a counter, either setting a marker word or running a routine.

name: loop_until_status_flags
description: Repeatedly calls drawing and timing routines, choosing between two routines based on a counter and a one-time marker, until either of two status words becomes non-zero. It then clears the marker and returns the first status word.

name: get_shared_table_address
description: Returns the address of a fixed table inside the shared data area, computed from the base pointer by a constant offset.

name: init_dos_library_or_alert
description: Clears 849 longwords of shared state and saves the stack base. It optionally calls a library routine when a flag bit is set, then opens the dos library through an exec routine, calling a second routine on success or the alert routine if the open fails.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Does nothing and returns immediately; it is an empty placeholder routine.

name: allocate_and_open_file_entry
description: Allocates an entry for the indexed file slot and fills its fields and a name tag. It then queries the current directory and the standard handles through the dos wrappers and opens the file in old-file mode, storing the result in the entry, or runs a cleanup call if the allocation fails.

name: split_text_into_argument_array
description: Copies a text buffer and splits it into tokens separated by spaces, tabs or line breaks. Double-quoted tokens are kept whole and a doubled quote inside them is treated as a literal quote. It then allocates a null-terminated array of pointers to the tokens, or sets the count to zero if the allocation fails.

name: copy_string_pad_zeros
description: Copies a null-terminated string into a destination of a given length, stopping at the terminator, then fills the rest of the destination with zero bytes. It returns the destination pointer.

name: append_string_bounded
description: Finds the terminating null of the destination, then appends the source string up to a limit of 32766 characters, writing a terminator if the copy was cut short. It returns the destination pointer.

name: append_string_with_limit
description: Finds the end of the destination string, then appends the source string until its terminator or until the count in the third argument runs out. If the copy stopped before the terminator, it writes a terminator after the last byte and returns the destination pointer.

name: copy_string_to_buffer
description: Copies a null-terminated string from the source into the destination, including the terminator, and returns the original destination pointer.

name: multiply_32_bit_low_product
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values from registers using 16-bit halves and returns the low 32 bits of the product in the upper half of the result. The second operand is returned unchanged in the lower half.

name: open_named_library_into_struct
description: Opens the library named by a global string through an exec routine, then looks up a second named library through it. It stores the returned pointers in the caller's structure and closes the first library before returning.

name: format_into_buffer_terminated
description: Saves a destination pointer in shared state, calls a formatting routine with the second argument and the caller's stack arguments, then writes a zero terminator at the destination and returns the result.

name: format_into_buffer_word_result
description: Does the same job as the terminated formatting wrapper, saving the destination pointer, formatting, and writing a zero terminator, but returns the formatter's result as a 16-bit value.

name: write_byte_to_output_buffer
description: Writes the low byte of its argument to the current position of the shared output pointer, advances that pointer by one byte and returns the byte.

name: format_arguments_to_output
description: Passes its argument and the caller's stack arguments to a shared formatting routine that uses the output callback, discarding the result.

name: call_two_subroutines_undecoded
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code is available for this routine. The facts show a 48-instruction routine that calls two other routines and is called from one place; its behaviour cannot be determined from this evidence.

name: emit_printf_formatted_text
description: Walks a format string, sending plain characters to an output callback and expanding each percent conversion. It handles flags, width, precision and length modifiers, converts character, decimal, string, octal, unsigned and hexadecimal arguments, and returns the count written or -1 if the callback fails.

name: negate_result_by_input_signs
description: Takes two signed inputs and records whether their signs differ. It calls a routine and negates the value it returns when the signs differ, then returns that value together with the second input.

name: negate_result_if_first_negative
description: Calls a routine and negates its second returned value when the first input is negative. It returns that value together with the unchanged second input register.

name: call_and_pass_through_second
description: Calls a routine and returns its second register result together with the unchanged second input register.

name: forward_call_no_arguments
description: Calls one routine with no arguments and returns. It performs no other work, so it acts as a pass-through wrapper.

name: divide_32_bit_quotient_remainder
description: Divides two 32-bit values and returns the quotient and remainder together. When the divisor exceeds 16 bits it uses a sixteen-step shift-and-subtract loop; otherwise it divides using 16-bit operations on the low half.

name: compute_string_length
description: Walks a zero-terminated byte string until its terminator and returns the number of bytes before it. It does not change memory.

name: forward_call_single_routine
description: Calls one routine with no arguments and returns. Its entry is referenced by address, so it is reached indirectly.

name: call_three_routines_undecoded
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code is available for this routine. The facts show a 21-instruction routine that calls three other routines, is called from two places and is referenced by address; its behaviour cannot be determined from this evidence.

name: stub_empty_return_callback
description: Does nothing and returns immediately. Its entry is referenced by address, so it is used as an empty callback.

name: call_two_routines_undecoded
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code is available for this routine. The facts show a 15-instruction routine that calls two other routines, is called from two places and is referenced by address; its behaviour cannot be determined from this evidence.

name: write_byte_and_advance_pointer
description: Reads a byte from a fixed offset within a base block, writes it to the destination pointer held in a register, advances that pointer by one byte and returns the byte.

name: call_routine_over_address_range
description: Calls a routine for each address from a base-relative start up to a fixed limit, stepping 22 bytes each time.

name: flush_and_reset_stream_buffer
description: Returns minus one for a null stream. Otherwise it flushes pending data when a buffer flag is set, releases the buffers if their flags are set, then clears the stream's pointer, count and flag fields. It returns the combined result of the flush calls.

name: flush_stream_buffer_registers
description: Operates on a stream block passed in a register: it flushes pending data when a flag is set, releases buffers if flagged, then clears the stream's pointer, count and flag fields and returns the flush result.

name: write_byte_to_buffered_stream
description: Writes one byte to a buffered stream. It returns minus one once the stream's error flag is set; otherwise it flushes or allocates the buffer as needed and stores the byte when there is room, resetting the stream and returning minus one if the write cannot be completed.

name: put_byte_via_register_stream
description: Writes one byte to a buffered stream whose block is passed in a register. It returns minus one on error, otherwise it flushes or allocates the buffer as needed and stores the byte when there is room, resetting the stream and returning minus one if the write fails.

name: write_byte_direct_or_buffered
description: Writes one byte to a stream. If the stream's error field is minus one it returns minus one; if no buffer exists it allocates one. When the stream's size field equals one it passes the byte through a write routine, otherwise it stores the byte at the current buffer position.

name: write_byte_with_stream_mode
description: Writes one byte to a stream: it allocates a buffer if none exists, and when the stream's size field equals one it passes the byte through a write routine. Otherwise it stores the byte at the current buffer position and returns the byte, or minus one if the pass-through write fails.

name: store_byte_in_stream_buffer
description: Stores one byte at the stream's current buffer position, advances that position, sets the stream's buffered flag and returns the stored byte.

name: allocate_free_pool_entry
description: Scans a fixed pool of 22-byte entries for one whose flag byte is clear, zeroes its first three words and returns it. It returns null when every entry is in use.

name: allocate_pool_entry_from_register
description: Searches the same kind of 22-byte entry pool, starting from a pointer held in a register. It zeroes the first three words of a free entry and returns it, or returns null when none is free.

name: clear_pool_entry_words
description: Zeroes the first three longwords of the entry whose address is held in a register.

name: init_stream_buffer_descriptor
description: Tries to obtain a buffer. If none is available it sets the buffer size to one and points at an inline area inside the structure; otherwise it sets the size to 1024, stores the buffer pointer, marks it allocated, and sets a further flag when a follow-up call returns non-zero.

name: init_shared_buffer_descriptor
description: Sets the buffer size to 1024 and marks the buffer as allocated, pointing it at a shared buffer address held in shared state. It then calls a routine and sets a further flag if that call returns non-zero.

name: free_all_pool_entries
description: Walks a linked list starting at a head pointer in shared state, releasing each node through a release routine with its size plus eight. It then clears the head pointer and returns zero.

name: free_entries_list_from_register
description: Walks a linked list whose head is held in a register, releasing each node through a release routine with its size plus eight, then clears the shared head pointer and returns zero.

name: allocate_tracked_memory_block
description: Allocates a block of the requested size plus eight bytes through an allocation routine. On success it links the block at the head of a shared list and returns the address after its eight-byte header; it returns null on failure.

name: link_block_at_list_head
description: Links a block held in a register at the head of a shared list, storing the previous head in its first word and its size in its second word. It returns the address after the eight-byte header.

name: forward_low_word_argument
description: Passes the low 16 bits of its argument to a routine and returns. It performs no other operation.

name: unlink_and_free_tracked_block
description: Searches the shared list for the block whose header matches the parameter. If found it unlinks the block, releases it through a release routine with its size plus eight and returns zero; otherwise it returns minus one.

name: unlink_block_by_register_key
description: Searches a list whose head is held in a register for the block that matches a structure pointer. If found it unlinks and releases that block and returns zero, or it returns minus one when no block matches.

name: unlink_node_from_list
description: Removes a node from a list by writing its successor into the previous node, or into the shared head when the node was first. It then calls a routine and returns zero.

name: pop_head_and_release
description: Sets the shared list head to the successor of the node held in a register, calls a release routine and returns zero.

name: check_table_entry_and_call
description: Checks that an index is in range and that its table entry is set. If not it records error code 2 and returns minus one; otherwise it calls a routine with the entry and returns one when that call is non-zero, zero otherwise.

name: test_table_entry_result
description: Looks up a table entry from an index argument, passes it to a routine and returns true when that routine returns non-zero.

name: stub_return_zero_handler
description: Returns zero and does nothing else; it is a placeholder handler referenced by address.

name: delete_file_store_error
description: Calls a delete routine with its argument. On failure it stores the DOS error code and returns minus one; otherwise it returns zero.

name: stub_return_zero_callback
description: Returns zero and does nothing else; it is a placeholder callback referenced by address.

name: call_two_routines_undecoded
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code is available for this routine. The facts show a 19-instruction routine that calls two other routines, is called from five places and is referenced by address; its behaviour cannot be determined from this evidence.

name: check_file_mode_then_call
description: Returns minus one and records error code 5 when the handle's mode bits are clear. Otherwise it calls a routine with the handle and two fields from the caller's data, and if that call returns minus one it stores the DOS error code and returns minus one.

name: write_record_store_error
description: Calls a routine with the handle and two fields from the caller's data. When that call returns minus one it stores the DOS error code and returns minus one; otherwise it returns the routine's result.

name: stub_empty_return_handler
description: Does nothing and returns; it is an empty handler referenced by address.

name: poll_mask_bit_then_call
description: Calls a routine with a fixed mask and tests bit 12 of its result. If the bit is set and a stored flag is zero it returns the result; if the bit is set and the flag is non-zero it calls a second routine. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: call_then_return_zero
description: Calls a routine and returns zero. It is referenced by address and does nothing else.

name: write_fixed_message_to_output
description: Obtains a pointer from a routine using a constant and a length of four, writes the result to the output stream through a routine, then calls a library routine. The facts show output and write wrappers are used.

name: call_optional_handler_then_routine
description: Calls a stored handler when its pointer is set, then calls one routine and returns.

name: release_resources_and_return_status
description: Frees a stored array after calling a routine for each of its entries, runs a stored cleanup handler and releases up to three further stored blocks. It calls a library routine when a flag bit is set, finishes by releasing the remaining blocks or list, and returns the value held in its saved stack slot.

name: release_resources_under_supervisor
description: Loops over a table, releases the stored array and block, and runs a cleanup handler. When a flag bit is set it calls a library routine in supervisor state, then releases a stored list and returns the value held in its saved stack slot.

name: release_stored_list_blocks
description: When a stored list pointer is set, releases its block through a release routine with a size computed from the stored count, and releases the secondary block. It returns the value held in its saved stack slot.

name: call_cleanup_then_return_slot
description: Calls one routine, passes a stored value to a second routine, and returns the value held in its saved stack slot.

name: release_indexed_table_entry
description: Checks that an index is in range and that its table entry is set, otherwise recording error code 2 and returning minus one. It releases the entry through a routine unless its flag bit is set, clears the entry and returns zero.

name: release_entry_and_clear
description: Calls a routine on the stored entry unless its flag bit is set, then clears the entry and returns zero.

name: call_stored_handler_slot
description: Calls the handler stored at a fixed negative offset from a base pointer held in shared state. The jump target could not be recovered, so the handler it reaches is not known.

name: call_second_stored_handler
description: Calls the handler stored at another fixed negative offset from the same base pointer. The jump target could not be recovered, so the handler it reaches is not known.

name: call_lock_handler_slot
description: Calls a DOS-library function through a handler slot at a fixed negative offset from a base pointer. The jump target could not be recovered from the decompiled jump table, so this is described from the wrapper it reaches, which the facts identify as the lock call.

name: call_open_handler_slot
description: Calls a DOS-library function through a handler slot at a fixed negative offset from a base pointer. The jump target could not be recovered from the decompiled jump table, so this is described from the wrapper it reaches, which the facts identify as the open call.

name: call_read_handler_slot
description: Calls a DOS-library function through a handler slot at a fixed negative offset from a base pointer. The jump target could not be recovered from the decompiled jump table, so this is described from the wrapper it reaches, which the facts identify as the read call.

name: call_unlock_handler_slot
description: Calls a DOS-library function through a handler slot at a fixed negative offset from a base pointer. The jump target could not be recovered from the decompiled jump table, so this is described from the wrapper it reaches, which the facts identify as the unlock call.

name: call_write_handler_slot
description: Calls a DOS-library function through a handler slot at a fixed negative offset from a base pointer. The jump target could not be recovered from the decompiled jump table, so this is described from the wrapper it reaches, which the facts identify as the write call.

name: call_supervisor_library_slot
description: Calls a library routine through a handler slot at a fixed negative offset from a base pointer. The facts show the same offset is used by the supervisor-state call elsewhere in the program.

name: allocate_and_init_record_entry
description: Looks up a free index, returning zero if none exists, and allocates a cleared 34-byte record. It fills the record with the first parameter, the flag byte, a type code of 4, a zero byte and the index, stores a value from a routine, then links the record and returns it. If the allocation fails it releases the index and returns zero.

name: allocate_and_init_record_from_params
description: Allocates a cleared 34-byte record through the allocator and fills it from the caller's fields: a value, a flag byte, a type code of 4 and a zero byte. It stores a value from a routine, then links the record or passes it to a routine, returning the record. If the allocation fails it releases nothing and returns zero.

name: fill_record_entry_fields
description: Fills an existing 34-byte record with a value, a flag byte, a type code of 4 and a zero byte, stores a value from a routine, then calls a routine on the record or on its trailing field.

name: process_record_trailing_field
description: Passes the address of a field 20 bytes into a record held in a register to a routine, then returns.

name: release_record_entry
description: Releases a 34-byte record. If its first field is set it calls a routine on the record, then marks its type byte and a trailing field as invalid, calls a routine with the flag byte, and frees the block using its size.

name: call_routine_with_constant_48
description: Calls a routine with its argument and the constant 48, then returns.

name: forward_argument_to_routine
description: Passes its pointer argument to a routine and returns; it does nothing else.

name: allocate_type5_record
description: If the given pointer is non-zero, allocates a cleared block through the allocator and stores a type code of 5, a word from the second argument and the pointer in it. It returns the block, or zero when the input is zero or the allocation fails.

name: release_record_with_size_field
description: If the record pointer is set, marks its type byte and two trailing fields as invalid and frees the block using the size stored in its word field, returning the free result. A null pointer returns zero.

name: call_library_slot_198
description: Calls a library function through a handler slot 198 bytes below a base pointer held in shared state. The target is not recovered from the decompiled jump table.

name: call_library_slot_294
description: Calls a library function through a handler slot 294 bytes below a base pointer held in shared state. The target is not recovered from the decompiled jump table.

name: call_library_slot_132
description: Calls a library function through a handler slot 132 bytes below a base pointer held in shared state. The target is not recovered from the decompiled jump table.

name: call_library_slot_210
description: Calls a library function through a handler slot 210 bytes below a base pointer held in shared state. The target is not recovered from the decompiled jump table.

name: initialize_list_head_pointers
description: Initialises a list head in the block at its argument: the first word points four bytes past the head, the second word is cleared and the third word points back to the head itself.

name: call_library_slot_552
description: Calls a library function through a handler slot 552 bytes below a base pointer held in shared state. The target is not recovered from the decompiled jump table.

name: read_disk_track_with_sync
description: Allocates a buffer through the library allocator, starts a disk DMA read into it and waits for its first word to match an expected sync value. The disk motor and DMA control registers are set before the read and the routine calls a finishing routine when the match is found. If the allocation fails or the sync value is not found, it halts by writing to address zero and jumping to an invalid address.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:L/Disk-Validator:0:0000
name: initialise_validation_state_entry
description: Entry point of the disk validation program. It formats a two-character status string from counters, initialises several counters and a fill table with all-ones values, then starts a loop over block bit masks. The pseudo-code is truncated partway through, so only the setup stage is visible.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:0000
name: clear_block_and_store_pointers
description: Clears 951 longwords starting at a computed block address, then stores a pointer and a global value into fixed slots of the same structure and calls a routine.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:016E
name: setup_graphics_and_trackdisk
description: Opens the libraries and device named in its text and allocates the resources they need, recording a flag bit for each one acquired. It sets up several list heads and two structures of fixed size, and returns a distinct failure code for each setup step that fails.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:08BA
name: release_resources_by_flags
description: Checks a set of flag bytes and, for each set bit, releases a stored block through a release routine with its fixed size. It then closes the stored library and device handles, releases list entries, clears the flag byte and returns.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:0B36
name: build_six_entry_offset_table
description: Calls a routine with the constant 920 and a block pointer, then initialises a structure. It walks a block of length-prefixed records six times, storing a pointer and length for each into two six-entry tables.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:0BCC
name: open_tile_at_position
description: Checks the tile at a given position and its neighbours for a lookup value of 15, then searches a 17-entry table for a matching entry. It rewrites tile bytes around the position according to that entry and sets a flag, returning 1 on success and 0 when no entry matches. The referenced messages It opened and It's locked show the result text it is associated with.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:0EEE
name: initialize_display_and_input
description: Runs a long start-up sequence that initialises several structures and five pointer-plus-offset entries, then sets display and text parameters through indirect calls. Its referenced text includes No Arrows, hiscreen and page0, and it loads and shows the named screens. The pseudo-code is truncated partway through, so the rest of the routine is not visible.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:5778
name: update_scroll_and_step_row
description: Updates two position offsets by the difference between the new and previous coordinates, then stores the coordinates as the new previous values. It optionally recomputes an index from them, then calls a routine repeatedly and steps the vertical coordinate each time it returns non-zero, stopping at zero.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:585C
name: find_region_and_update_state
description: Repeatedly selects a region table from a global counter and searches it for an entry whose bounds contain the current coordinates. It derives a state value from that entry with conditional adjustments, and calls a callback with a slot argument when the state changes.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:5B7E
name: update_animation_state
description: Combines the result of a routine with a byte from the entry to produce a new byte, then looks up a table value for the current state. When that value changes it resets a counter and calls a routine with the new state.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:5C00
name: place_entry_at_free_position
description: Tries up to fifteen positions near a base point, rejecting any that fail a check routine. It then fills the chosen record with its position, a type value, flags and table-derived fields, and returns one, or zero if no position passes the check.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:5DF0
name: update_entity_record_state
description: For the entry selected by a global index whose state is idle, sets its timing and state bytes to fixed values and adjusts counters. It calls routines depending on its type and, when the parameter is zero, calls a routine with the second argument.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:5EBA
name: set_state_and_timing
description: Sets a state byte to 6 when the parameter is 10 and to 5 otherwise. If the stored state differs from the parameter it updates the state and calls routines to apply it, then sets position offsets from table values, clears several flag bytes and stores the parameter in the state fields.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:5F98
name: initialise_stage_state_display
description: Clears a set of state variables, then either makes a single routine call when its parameter is zero or sets up the current stage from a table of starting coordinates. The stage setup clears a 31-byte area, loads display resources and shows a stage-specific view with pauses between steps. The pseudo-code is truncated partway through.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:638C
name: set_display_offsets_from_param
description: Calls two routines, then stores display offsets derived from its parameter and a routine result: several words are set to 160 minus the parameter and others to 100 and 95 minus the result. It also calls a routine with computed offsets and a global address, then calls a routine with no arguments.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:643C
name: draw_sprite_from_index
description: Chooses a base index from state values and position checks, using 24, 16, 20, 8 or 4. It then passes the four table entries starting at that index to a drawing routine, choosing one of two routines according to a flag bit and the parameter.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:6544
name: update_zone_index_from_position
description: When a state value is below eight, computes a zone index from the two position words. If the zone changed it records the new zone and calls a routine, otherwise it stores the state. It then checks two pointers through a routine and, when they are set or a counter is high, derives two offset values from the zone index before calling a routine with two position values.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:6670
name: swap_buffer_pointers
description: Swaps two stored pointers, copies the first two words of the new current buffer into a global pair, and calls routines with pointers to the buffers. It restores the second word of the current buffer, then calls one more routine.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:66C6
name: open_input_device_request
description: Creates a message port and an I/O request, then opens the input device with that request. It releases the port and returns zero if the request cannot be created; otherwise it sets up the request and returns one only when the device open succeeds.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:6776
name: close_input_request_and_port
description: Sets a field of the I/O request to 10 and a pointer field, makes three routine calls with the request and then one routine call with the port handle.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:67BC
name: render_twelve_entry_slots
description: Walks a table of 18-byte stage entries and records the index of each flagged entry in a 12-slot array, calling a routine for each. It then fills the remaining slots: for each one it alternates two constants, obtains a value from a routine, draws a line with it and marks the slot with a filler value.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:68DA
name: render_slot_line
description: Looks up a value for a slot from a table, adjusted for the current stage, then sets the drawing parameters and draws two entries at computed offsets. It draws a third item either from an offset table or at a position computed from the stage value.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:6A76
name: dispatch_stage_event_by_value
description: A switch on a stage value that dispatches events. The first case handles one message and, for a parameter of 5, loops over 31 entries to draw items with values from tables and sets flags; other cases call routines for further messages. The pseudo-code is truncated, so the remaining cases are not visible.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:7EAC
name: retry_check_then_notify
description: Calls a routine up to 25 times, stopping early when a test on the stored coordinates returns 5. If the loop did not stop early it calls a routine with the coordinates and then calls the notifier with code 5.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:7EF2
name: notify_position_event
description: Calls a routine with the value 1 and the stored coordinates, then calls the notifier with code 5.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:7F1A
name: set_stage_and_refresh
description: When a flag bit is clear, stores its parameter as the current stage value, clears a byte and calls a routine. Otherwise it returns without effect.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:7F3A
name: load_font_metric_tables
description: Fills two seven-entry arrays by calling a routine with offsets, then fills a six-byte array while noting whether a newline value appears, which sets a line height of 10 instead of 8. It stores several single-byte values derived from routine results into shared globals.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:7FE8
name: wait_until_counter_reaches_ten
description: Calls a routine repeatedly while a 16-bit counter is below ten. It does not change the counter itself.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:7FFC
name: apply_record_state_for_index
description: When the index is below ten, it compares several fields of that record with cached values and calls update routines for any that changed. It then checks four slot values and, on a change, refreshes five entries and caches the value. It clears a flag across seven entries, stores the index as the previous state and sets the counter to ten.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:827A
name: call_routine_if_flag_set
description: When a flag bit is set, calls a stored routine with a value from a table indexed by the first argument, a shifted value from a second table and the second argument. Otherwise it does nothing.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:82BA
name: initialize_text_and_stage_pointers
description: Calls a routine three times with three buffer addresses and the value 35, then sets a stored pointer from a table indexed by the stage value minus one. It finishes by calling a routine with another buffer address and the value 60.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:830E
name: store_stack_argument_in_field
description: Stores the value passed on the stack into the longword at offset four of the structure held in a register.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:8314
name: update_linked_object_list
description: Walks a linked list of object records. Type-one records copy a byte from a table into a 128-entry ring buffer, and type-two records update an index and byte code from their coordinates. Each record's offsets are added to its position, clamped to fixed screen bounds, and a callback is called when one is set.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:836A
name: update_linked_objects_unrolled
description: Performs the same linked-list update as its neighbour, with the type-one and type-two branches written as jump-based code. It clamps positions to the same bounds and calls the callback when one is set.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:8396
name: update_linked_objects_with_table
description: Walks the same kind of object list, copying byte codes from a table for type-one records and computing byte codes from coordinates for type-two records. It clamps positions to fixed bounds and calls a callback when one is set.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:84C4
name: dequeue_ring_buffer_byte
description: Returns the next queued byte from a 128-entry ring buffer and advances the read index. It returns zero when the buffer is empty, and the result is combined with the second register unchanged.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:84EE
name: advance_generator_and_mix
description: Multiplies the stored 16-bit state by a constant and adds one, stores the result as the new state, and returns a rotated and masked view of that value.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:8506
name: mask_parameter_with_routine
description: Calls a routine and returns its result combined with the parameter by bitwise AND.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:850E
name: return_routine_low_bit
description: Calls a routine and returns only its lowest bit.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:8518
name: return_routine_low_two_bits
description: Calls a routine and returns only the lowest two bits of its result.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:8522
name: return_routine_low_three_bits
description: Calls a routine and returns only the lowest three bits of its result.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:852C
name: return_routine_low_six_bits
description: Calls a routine and returns only the lowest six bits of its result.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:8536
name: return_routine_low_byte
description: Calls a routine and returns its low byte.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:8540
name: modulo_routine_result_by_parameter
description: Calls a routine and returns the remainder of its low 16 bits divided by the low 16 bits of the parameter, combined with the parameter unchanged.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:8554
name: call_routine_then_library_slot
description: Calls a routine, then calls the library function at a fixed offset from a stored library base, and returns its two input registers unchanged.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:8580
name: format_decimal_into_buffer
description: Writes the value in the first register as decimal digits into a ten-character buffer, right-aligned, and fills the leading positions with spaces.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:8588
name: format_decimal_with_width
description: Writes the 16-bit value as decimal digits into a buffer ending at the index held in the second register, moving left one character per digit. Once the value reaches zero it fills the remaining positions with spaces.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:85A4
name: fill_spaces_to_index
description: Writes space characters into a buffer from the index in a register down to position zero inclusive.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:85D0
name: run_nested_routine_loops
description: Runs three nested loops with counts of 17, 16 and 5. Each innermost step calls four table-indexed routines, with an extra pair of calls while the outer count is above nine, and returns its input registers unchanged.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:86D4
name: process_text_segments
description: Walks a null-terminated string. A byte with its high bit set triggers a callback through a function pointer; otherwise it measures the run of plain characters up to the next null or high-bit byte and passes that segment, with its length, to a routine that takes many arguments from registers and shared globals.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:8728
name: sample_tile_nibble_at_position
description: Computes a bit mask from the two input values and looks up a byte in a map using coordinates offset by stored values. It tests a table byte against the mask and returns the high nibble of an associated byte when the test passes, or zero otherwise.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:8730
name: sample_map_nibble_from_registers
description: Performs the same map sampling as its neighbour, taking its two inputs from registers instead of arguments.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:87C8
name: call_routine_and_decrement_counter
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer stored in shared state, then decrements a stored 32-bit counter by four.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a].adf:fmain:0:87EA
name: call_routine_and_subtract_counter
description: Calls the same routine through the function pointer, then subtracts from a stored 32-bit counter the sum of another stored value and four.
